agent_messages:
Factor the zeta pole as \(\zeta(s)=g(s)/(s-1)\), where \(g\) is holomorphic and nonzero near \(1\). Then
\[
-\frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)}-\frac1{s-1}=-\frac{g'(s)}{g(s)},
\]
so the apparent singularity is removable and the expression is locally bounded. Independently, the standard zero-count estimate \(N(T)=O(T\log T)\), together with \(\log T=O(\sqrt T)\) for \(T\ge2\), yields the stated \(T^{3/2}\) bound.
